summary_paragraph: A  female patient with a history of paraplegia, neurogenic bladder, and recurrent UTIs was admitted for flank pain, dysuria, and subjective fever after being unable to change her urinary catheter for over three weeks. She was treated initially with ceftriaxone, but due to the isolation of Serratia marcescens in her urine culture and the risk of developing resistance, her antibiotic was switched to ciprofloxacin for a complete 14-day course. Her catheter was changed during admission, and she showed clinical improvement with resolution of infection markers and stabilization of mild acidosis. She also had fecal impaction managed with a bowel regimen, and her nausea was controlled with antiemetics. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to complete antibiotics, maintain catheter hygiene, follow up with urology, and continue bowel and nausea medications as needed.
problems: Infection and inflammatory reaction due to indwelling urinary catheter
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Cauda equina syndrome with neurogenic bladder
Late effect of spinal cord injury
